name: LC-130H Hercules (ski)
description: Ski-equipped Hercules, the workhorse of deep-field and South Pole resupply. Typical ski payload around 26,000 lb.

name: C-17A Globemaster III
description: Heavy wheeled airlifter for the intercontinental leg to ice or paved runways (e.g. Christchurch to McMurdo). Cannot land on snow.

name: Basler BT-67 (ski)
description: Turbine-converted DC-3 on skis. Long-range polar utility aircraft that reaches high plateau sites.

name: DHC-6 Twin Otter (ski)
description: Rugged STOL utility aircraft on wheel-skis for field camps and short, rough strips.

name: Airbus H125 (AS350 B3e)
description: Light single-engine helicopter with exceptional high-altitude performance; common for mountain and field support.

name: Bell 212
description: Medium twin-engine utility helicopter used for ship-to-shore and polar field work.

name: Bell 412EPX
description: Medium twin with a four-blade rotor; better hot-and-high performance than the 212.

name: Mi-8AMT / Mi-171
description: Medium-heavy transport helicopter; large cabin and sling loads for remote construction.

name: Heavy polar icebreaker
description: Breaks a channel through sea ice for cargo and fuel ships. Carries only limited cargo itself.

name: Ice-class cargo ship
description: Annual sealift of containers, vehicles and dry cargo, usually escorted by an icebreaker.

name: Ice-class fuel tanker
description: Delivers the season's bulk fuel (on the order of 20 million liters) to an ice pier or offshore hose.

name: Ice-strengthened research/supply vessel
description: Smaller vessel for personnel, science gear and light cargo to coastal stations.

name: Landing craft / barge
description: Shallow-draft craft for beach landings where there is no pier.

name: Heavy tractor traverse (per tractor-sled unit)
description: Tracked tractor towing a sled train of fuel bladders and cargo over groomed snow (e.g. a South Pole traverse).

name: Tracked over-snow vehicle
description: Sno-Cat/PistenBully-class vehicle for personnel and light cargo near the station.

name: 6×6 cargo truck (convoy unit)
description: All-terrain cargo truck for desert and mountain road convoys.

name: 4×4 utility vehicle
description: Light vehicle for personnel and small cargo on roads and tracks.
